internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: an imbuing treatment or quality that suffuses and characterizes what receives it
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The two tokens in 2:138 present God's sibgha as a defining imbuement or characterization. The food-context sibgh in 23:20 may denote a condiment; the verse does not itself establish that suffusion/characterization is the root residue there.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: The construct with God supplies the defining religious source in 2:138; the eater construction supplies culinary function in 23:20. These contextual roles must not be folded into the root.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 23:20:8:2 names sibgh for eaters and can be satisfied by condiment/relish without an explicit coloring or imbuing process.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: Both are forms of permeating coloration or treatment; this is plausible but not demonstrated within the culinary verse.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Tentatively distinct from simple color by profiling an applied, characterizing treatment; the food occurrence leaves that boundary uncertain.
internal_discovery.rationale: The divine-sibgha class supports the candidate, but one of three occurrences remains resistant.
